think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 56-year-old rural resident and chronic smoker presents with severe weight loss (17 kg), dysphagia with a friable esophageal ulcer, craniocervical cutaneous lesions, and acute hypoxemic respiratory failure associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection. Imaging demonstrates extensive multisystem disease: cavitary consolidations with ground-glass infiltrates, necrotic mesenteric/gastrohepatic lymphadenopathy, bilateral adrenal thickening, and ring-enhancing brain lesions. This clinical constellation creates acute diagnostic tension between disseminated malignancy (esophageal or lung carcinoma with widespread metastases), disseminated tuberculosis, and a disseminated endemic dimorphic fungal infection unmasked or exacerbated by viral respiratory infection.

2. Admission Breakpoint: Clinical evaluation concludes after initial history, physical examination, triage laboratories (hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, leukocytosis, thrombocytosis, marked CRP elevation of 288 mg/dL, negative HIV), and comprehensive CT imaging (chest, abdomen, and brain), strictly prior to the return of esophageal biopsy histology, sputum mycobacterial testing/cultures, lymph node excision, and specific fungal serology.

3. Differential Distinctions: Disseminated tuberculosis is excluded by negative sputum AFB smears, cultures, and M. tuberculosis PCR. Metastatic neoplasm is ruled out by the absence of malignant cells on histopathology. The diagnosis of disseminated paracoccidioidomycosis is confirmed by Grocott silver staining demonstrating characteristic fungal yeast forms in lymph node and esophageal biopsies along with high-titer seropositivity (1:128).
case_prompt:
A 56-year-old male who had resided in a rural area of São Paulo State for over 30 years presented to the medical center with a 3-month history of progressive dyspepsia and dysphagia, accompanied by an unintentional 17-kg weight loss and the emergence of multiple skin lesions over his face and head. He also reported a persistent dry cough of at least 1 year's duration, which he had attributed to a 15 pack-year smoking history. A recent outpatient upper digestive endoscopy had demonstrated an ulcerated lesion of the esophagus with ill-defined margins that was friable to the touch, with endoscopic mucosal tissue sampling performed. Prior to presentation, his shortness of breath worsened acutely, and he tested positive for SARS-CoV-2.

On physical examination, the patient was in respiratory distress. Ambient air oxygen saturation was 84%, blood pressure was 100/60 mmHg, heart rate was 82 beats per minute, and respiratory rate was 20 breaths per minute. Cutaneous examination revealed multiple ulcerative and crusted lesions distributed across the temporomandibular region, lower lip, ear lobe, right nasal ala, and jaw. No peripheral lymphadenopathy was palpable on initial examination.

Initial laboratory evaluation revealed a hemoglobin level of 12.1 g/dL, white blood cell count of 12,300/mm³, platelet count of 447,000/mm³, and C-reactive protein markedly elevated at 288 mg/dL. Screening serology for HIV was negative.

Computed tomography (CT) of the chest demonstrated extensive pulmonary consolidations in the right upper lobe and bilaterally in the lower lobes—several showing cavitation—along with diffuse ground-glass opacities, interlobular septal thickening, and a small right-sided pleural effusion. Abdominal CT revealed multiple necrotic mesenteric and gastrohepatic lymph nodes measuring up to 3.7 cm in diameter, as well as bilateral nodular adrenal gland thickening. Cranial CT demonstrated multiple ring-enhancing parenchymal lesions, most prominent within the splenium of the left corpus callosum.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Cavitary upper lobe pulmonary consolidations, necrotic intra-abdominal adenopathy, bilateral adrenal enlargement, and multiple ring-enhancing intracranial lesions strongly raised suspicion for disseminated tuberculosis; however, sputum acid-fast bacilli smear, mycobacterial culture, and targeted PCR were all negative.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The sputum culture and acid-fast bacilli smear yielded negative results, as well as the PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Disseminated / Metastatic Esophageal or Pulmonary Carcinoma
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: A friable, irregular esophageal ulcer in a chronic smoker with severe weight loss, massive necrotic lymphadenopathy, adrenal nodules, and multiple ring-enhancing brain lesions raised high suspicion for advanced malignancy with systemic metastasis; however, histopathology of both the esophageal ulcer and subsequent lymph node biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation with yeast structures rather than malignant cells.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: He underwent a digestive endoscopy, which revealed no specific alterations in his stomach and duodenum but did show an esophageal ulcerated lesion with imprecise limits, friable to the touch.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic pivot occurred when submandibular lymph node biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation with characteristic yeast forms on Grocott staining, concordant with esophageal biopsy findings and confirmed by specific serology titer of 1:128, establishing chronic multifocal disseminated paracoccidioidomycosis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A lymph node biopsy revealed a granulomatous inflammation and the Grocott stain technique revealed structures compatible with Paracoccidioides sp. infection.

editor_comments: Distilled in strict adherence to Stanford MedCaseReasoning methodology. Admission prompt cleanly stops before biopsy histology and confirmatory serology/cultures return, removing all pathogen markers and diagnostic labels. Verbatim quotes from the published case text substantiate each differential step.
